claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine lamellar fcc/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
The as-cast alloy has a moderate balance of strength and ductility.
Post-solidification aging can induce controlled coherent nanoprecipitation within a lamellar phase of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Aging-induced coherent nanoprecipitation will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Aging between 400 and 600 degrees Celsius is sufficiently low-temperature to preserve the lamellar architecture.
Calibrating aging duration can produce a uniform nanoscale precipitate distribution without coarsening.
The proposed strength-ductility benefit should hold at room temperature and moderate service temperatures.
The aging treatment will form fine, coherent, NiAl-rich particles embedded within the ductile fcc phase.
The aging treatment will maintain an optimal interlamellar spacing.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and stress relief will preserve or enhance ductility.
Optimized aging will increase yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
The appropriate baseline is untreated as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Overaging, precipitate coarsening, loss of coherent interfaces, or disruption of the lamellar structure will negate the proposed improvements.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes overaged, coarsened, or incoherent precipitate conditions from the regime where the benefit is expected, but the falsification rule treats coarsening and loss of coherence as falsifying outcomes rather than excluded processing failures.
